text:
omar: Heads-up — bringing up helix35b (35B) int4 canary on dedicated cluster. Seeing reproducible OOMs when batch_size >= 5 + max_new_tokens >= 512. Anyone who touched kv/prefetch defaults recently?

maya: saw the alerts, dug into one failure. stack trace shows allocation spike during kv cache growth, fragmentation then cuda OOM. log excerpt: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.9 GiB (GPU 0; 80.00 GiB total capacity; 72.1 GiB already allocated)
Trace: serve/runtime/prefetcher.py:142 -> kv/cache.py:88
```

omar: config we used: quant=int4, group=128, prefetch=true, kv_reserve=0.15, batch_size=8, max_new_tokens=512. Canary runs on A100-80GB.

leo: hmm group=128 on int4 could increase peak memory for qkv kernels, but fragmentation smell points to dynamic KV growth. Are we evicting old sessions?

maya: evict policy is LRU but we only trigger after hitting 0.92 of reserved. With kv_reserve=0.15 and extra allocation from quant kernels we cross threshold mid-generation.

sara: immediate mitigation — reduce default max_new_tokens to 256 for helix35b canary and force batch_size <=4 while we debug. Also propose kv_reserve=0.10 for the canary to reduce held overhead.

mike: agree. Another lightweight fix: disable prefetching for helix35b in canary. Prefetching gives latency win but increases transient pages. Set `prefetch.window=0` in model config.

jen: quick quality check: we ran a 1k sample eval vs fp16 baseline — int4 shows ~0.7% BLEU drop and 1.8% EM drop on our internal SQuAD-like set. Not huge but worth noting if we change tokens defaults (shorter + fewer retries might hide regressions).

omar: thanks. Action items I will do now: 1) patch model catalog for helix35b canary: `max_new_tokens: 256`, `batch_limit: 4`, `prefetch: false`, `kv_reserve: 0.10`; 2) run 1000-sample perf sweep; 3) create canary with rollout policy 5% traffic.

ci-bot: Deploy queued: canary/helix35b-int4-config-2026-03-20-omar. CI checks passed.

infra-bot: Canary spin-up started on pool-gpu-a100-07 (3 replicas).

mike: while that's happening, let's try a small code change: add soft-kv-trim to runtime. Pseudocode: 
```
if (kv.size > kv_limit * 0.9) {
  trim_amount = ceil(kv.size * 0.12)
  kv.evict(trim_amount)
}
```
This prevents big sudden evictions and reduces fragmentation. I'll attach a PR in 15m.

leo: also look at allocation alignment in the allocator — 256B granularities lead to slack for int4 buffers. Might shrink default alignment for quant paths.

maya: ran quick perf after lowering max_new_tokens locally: no OOM on same inputs with batch=6 and max_new_tokens=256. Latency increased slightly (~4% tail), but stable.

omar: good. I'll monitor the canary results and post metrics. If canary is stable for 30m we'll promote and then open follow-up to test soft-kv-trim + allocator alignment changes in a separate rollout.

jen: note for release notes: mention quality delta and change in default max_new_tokens for helix35b canary. tagging product for visibility. :eyes:

sara: filing the follow-up ticket: MLINF-4721 "helix35b: allocator alignment + soft-kv-trim to reduce fragmentation". Assign to infra/eng-ml.

omar: thanks all. ping me if you see any regressions or new OOM patterns. :thumbsup:
